subject: Agriculture
title: The Heavy Plow
description: A fast breakdown of The Heavy Plow for builders.

hook.text: Light scratch plows worked fine in Mediterranean soil. Northern Europe's heavy clay defeated them.

buildup.text: The heavy plow had a coulter to cut, a share to slice, and a moldboard to flip the soil over.

discovery.text: It broke through dense clay and turned it into productive farmland. Northern Europe could finally feed itself.

twist.text: Heavy plows needed eight oxen to pull. No single family owned that many—so farmers had to cooperate.

climax.text: The need to share oxen shaped medieval village life. Cooperation wasn't optional—it was survival.

punchline.text: A better plow didn't just turn soil. It built communities.

quiz.question: Why did the heavy plow require community cooperation?
options: It was too expensive to buy
It needed eight oxen, more than any family owned alone
